name: Jan Timman
milestone_by_age_26: Attained the Grandmaster title in 1974 at age 22, becoming the Netherlands' third Grandmaster after Max Euwe and Jan Hein Donner, and won the Dutch Chess Championship for the first time in the same year. By age 26 he had also won international tournaments at Hastings 1973-74, Sombor 1974, Netanya 1975, and Reykjavik 1976.
starting_point: Born in Amsterdam in 1951 to a mathematics professor father and a mother who had been a student of former world champion Max Euwe; learned chess from his older brother Ton, a FIDE Master.
current_position: Died on February 18, 2026 at age 74 in Arnhem, Netherlands; final role as one of the Netherlands' most celebrated chess grandmasters and chess authors.

trajectory.title: World Junior Championship bronze
trajectory.description: Finished third at the World Junior Chess Championship in Jerusalem at age 15, marking his emergence as an international talent.

trajectory.title: International Master title
trajectory.description: Awarded the International Master title by FIDE, establishing himself as a serious competitive player.

trajectory.title: Grandmaster title and first Dutch Championship
trajectory.description: Attained the Grandmaster title, becoming the Netherlands' third GM after Max Euwe and Jan Hein Donner, and won the Dutch Chess Championship for the first time.

trajectory.title: Reykjavik tournament victory
trajectory.description: Won the Reykjavik international tournament (shared with Fridrik Olafsson), continuing his string of international victories.

trajectory.title: World No. 2 ranking
trajectory.description: Reached the world No. 2 ranking on the FIDE list, behind only Anatoly Karpov, earning the moniker 'The Best of the West'.

trajectory.title: Won FIDE Interzonal in Taxco
trajectory.description: Won the Interzonal tournament in Taxco, qualifying for the Candidates cycle for the first time.

trajectory.title: FIDE World Championship challenger
trajectory.description: Lost the 1993 FIDE World Championship title match to Anatoly Karpov, the culmination of his quest for the chess crown.

trajectory.title: Ninth Dutch Championship
trajectory.description: Won his ninth and final Dutch Chess Championship, capping a dominant national career spanning over two decades.

trajectory.title: Death
trajectory.description: Died on February 18, 2026 in Arnhem, Netherlands, remembered as one of the greatest Western chess players of his era.

name: Ryuichi Sakamoto
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded the electronic band Yellow Magic Orchestra in 1978 at age 26 and released his debut solo album Thousand Knives of Ryuichi Sakamoto the same year, both becoming landmark works in electronic music history.
starting_point: Born in Tokyo in 1952 to a renowned editor father who shaped postwar Japanese literature; began piano at age three and studied composition at Tokyo National University of Fine Arts and Music.
current_position: Died on March 28, 2023 at age 71 in Tokyo, Japan; final role as an Oscar-winning composer and pioneering electronic musician.

trajectory.title: Professional debut as session musician
trajectory.description: Made his professional musical debut playing piano on an album by folk singer Tomobe Masato while still a university student.

trajectory.title: Studio musician and arranger
trajectory.description: Began working as a composer, arranger, and studio musician with major Japanese artists including Yamashita Tatsuro and Yano Akiko.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Yellow Magic Orchestra and debut solo album
trajectory.description: Co-founded YMO with Haruomi Hosono and Yukihiro Takahashi, and released debut solo album 'Thousand Knives of Ryuichi Sakamoto' the same year.

trajectory.title: B-2 Unit and 'Riot in Lagos'
trajectory.description: Released solo album B-2 Unit featuring 'Riot in Lagos,' a track that significantly influenced the development of electro, hip hop, and dance music.

trajectory.title: Film debut with 'Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence'
trajectory.description: Debuted as both actor and film composer in Nagisa Oshima's film co-starring David Bowie; the theme became an international hit.

trajectory.title: Academy Award for 'The Last Emperor'
trajectory.description: Won the Academy Award for Best Original Score for Bernardo Bertolucci's 'The Last Emperor,' becoming the first Japanese composer to win an Oscar.

trajectory.title: Barcelona Olympics ceremony
trajectory.description: Composed music for the opening ceremony of the 1992 Barcelona Summer Olympic Games.

trajectory.title: Score for 'The Revenant'
trajectory.description: Composed the acclaimed score for Alejandro Inarritu's 'The Revenant' (2015) while recovering from throat cancer diagnosis in 2014.

trajectory.title: Death
trajectory.description: Died on March 28, 2023 in Tokyo after a long battle with cancer, leaving behind a sprawling legacy across electronic, orchestral, and film music.

name: Alessandra Ambrosio
milestone_by_age_26: Booked the Millennium GUESS? campaign in Fall 2000 at age 19 and was hired by Victoria's Secret the same year, launching a career that made her a Victoria's Secret Angel from 2004 to 2017.
starting_point: Born in 1981 in Erechim, Brazil to gas station-owning parents of Italian and Polish-Brazilian descent; began modeling classes at age 12 and started modeling professionally at 15.
current_position: Continues modeling and has ventured into acting with appearances in films and television; resides in Los Angeles, California.

trajectory.title: Began modeling with Dilson Stein
trajectory.description: Started modeling professionally at age 15 after competing in Brazil's Elite Model Look competition.

trajectory.title: Millennium GUESS? campaign and Victoria's Secret debut
trajectory.description: Booked the Millennium GUESS? campaign in Fall 2000 and was hired by Victoria's Secret the same year, launching her international career.

trajectory.title: Victoria's Secret Angel and swimwear line
trajectory.description: Became a Victoria's Secret Angel and launched her own swimwear line, Alessandra Ambrosio by Sais, which sold 10,000 units in its first month.

trajectory.title: First PINK line spokesmodel
trajectory.description: Selected as the first spokesmodel for Victoria's Secret's PINK line, targeting younger consumers.

trajectory.title: London Olympics closing ceremony
trajectory.description: Represented Brazil in the 2012 London Olympics closing ceremony as part of the handover to Rio de Janeiro.

trajectory.title: Retired from Victoria's Secret
trajectory.description: Walked her final Victoria's Secret Fashion Show after 17 shows and 13 years as an Angel.

trajectory.title: Continued modeling and acting career
trajectory.description: Continues to model for major brands and has expanded into acting with roles in films and television shows.

name: Susan Polgár
milestone_by_age_26: Became the top-ranked female chess player in the world on the FIDE Elo rating list of July 1984 at age 15, the youngest ever to achieve the world #1 ranking. She won the World Under-16 Girls Championship in 1981 at age 12 and earned the Grandmaster title in 1991 at age 22.
starting_point: Born in Budapest, Hungary in 1969 to Laszlo Polgar, who deliberately educated his three daughters in chess from early childhood as an educational experiment; homeschooled with chess as the primary subject.
current_position: Lives in suburban St. Louis, Missouri; serves as head of the Susan Polgar Institute for Chess Excellence (SPICE) and coaches collegiate chess.

trajectory.title: World Under-16 Girls Championship
trajectory.description: Won the girls' division of the Under-16 World Youth Chess Championship at age 12.

trajectory.title: World #1 female player
trajectory.description: Became the top-ranked female chess player on the FIDE Elo rating list of July 1984, the youngest ever to achieve the world #1 ranking.

trajectory.title: Qualified for Men's World Championship
trajectory.description: Made history by qualifying for the Men's World Championship cycle but was denied entry due to her gender.

trajectory.title: Grandmaster title
trajectory.description: Became the third woman to earn the Grandmaster title by norms and rating, breaking the gender barrier in chess.

trajectory.title: Women's World Chess Champion
trajectory.description: Won the Women's World Chess Championship, becoming the first triple-crown winner in chess history.

trajectory.title: Olympiad leadership
trajectory.description: Led the United States to second place at the Chess Olympiad, going undefeated in 56 games on Board One.

trajectory.title: U.S. Chess Hall of Fame
trajectory.description: Inducted into the U.S. Chess Hall of Fame, followed by the World Chess Hall of Fame in 2023.

trajectory.title: Continued coaching and promotion
trajectory.description: Continues coaching collegiate chess and promoting chess education through the Susan Polgar Foundation and SPICE at Webster University.

name: Paul Breitner
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for Bayern Munich's senior team in 1970 at age 19, won the 1972 European Championship at 21, the 1974 FIFA World Cup at 22 (scoring in the final), and the 1974 European Cup, all before age 26.
starting_point: Born in Kolbermoor, Bavaria in 1951; began playing football at age six for SV Kolbermoor, later moving to ESV Freilassing where his father was his youth coach before joining Bayern Munich at 18.
current_position: Retired from football in 1983; works as a football commentator and pundit in Germany.

trajectory.title: Bayern Munich senior debut
trajectory.description: Debuted for Bayern Munich's senior team under coach Udo Lattek, quickly securing a regular starting spot as an attacking left-back.

trajectory.title: West Germany debut and DFB-Pokal
trajectory.description: Made his debut for West Germany and won the DFB-Pokal (German Cup) with Bayern Munich.

trajectory.title: European Championship winner
trajectory.description: Won the 1972 UEFA European Championship with West Germany, part of the dominant German team of the era.

trajectory.title: World Cup and European Cup double
trajectory.description: Won the 1974 FIFA World Cup (scoring in the final against the Netherlands) and the European Cup with Bayern Munich.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Real Madrid
trajectory.description: Moved to Real Madrid for over 1 million Deutsche Marks, forming a midfield partnership with Gunter Netzer and winning two La Liga titles.

trajectory.title: Return to Bayern Munich
trajectory.description: Returned to Bayern Munich after a season at Eintracht Braunschweig, transitioning to midfield and becoming one of the top midfielders of the early 1980s.

trajectory.title: German Footballer of the Year
trajectory.description: Named German Footballer of the Year after captaining Bayern to the Bundesliga title and leading the league in scoring from midfield.

trajectory.title: Retirement
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football in 1983 after a distinguished career with Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, and West Germany.

name: Roger Milla
milestone_by_age_26: Signed for top-division club Leopard Douala in 1970 at age 18 and won three Cameroonian championship titles, scoring 89 goals in 116 appearances over four years. Made Cameroon national team debut in 1973 and was African Footballer of the Year in 1976 at age 24.
starting_point: Born in Yaounde, Cameroon in 1952; began his football career with youth club Eclair de Douala before turning professional with Leopard Douala at age 18.
current_position: Retired from professional football in 1996 at age 44; involved in football development and humanitarian work in Cameroon.

trajectory.title: Signed for Leopard Douala
trajectory.description: Signed for top-division club Leopard Douala, winning three Cameroonian championship titles and scoring 89 goals in 116 appearances over four years.

trajectory.title: Cameroon national team debut
trajectory.description: Made his debut for the Cameroon national team, beginning a 21-year international career.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Tonnerre Yaounde
trajectory.description: Moved to Tonnerre Yaounde, scoring 69 goals in 87 games and winning the African Cup Winners' Cup.

trajectory.title: African Footballer of the Year
trajectory.description: Named African Footballer of the Year, the first major individual recognition of his career.

trajectory.title: Move to Europe with Valenciennes
trajectory.description: Moved to France to join Valenciennes, beginning a 12-year career in European football.

trajectory.title: French Cup winner with Monaco
trajectory.description: Won the French Cup with AS Monaco during his stint in French football.

trajectory.title: World Cup stardom
trajectory.description: Scored four goals at the 1990 FIFA World Cup at age 38, becoming the oldest goalscorer in World Cup history and helping Cameroon reach the quarter-finals as the first African team to do so.

trajectory.title: Oldest World Cup goalscorer record
trajectory.description: Broke his own record as the oldest goalscorer in World Cup history by scoring against Russia at the 1994 FIFA World Cup at age 42.

name: Michele Alboreto
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Formula Three Championship in 1980 (age 23-24), made his Formula One debut with Tyrrell at the 1981 San Marino Grand Prix (age 24), and won his first F1 Grand Prix at the 1982 Caesars Palace Grand Prix in Las Vegas (age 25), establishing himself as a rising star in motorsport.
starting_point: Born in Milan, Italy in 1956 to a small-business owner father with no motorsport background; built his first kart at 17 with his brother Carlo and began racing locally.
current_position: Died on April 25, 2001 at age 44 in a testing crash at the Lausitzring in Germany; final role as an Audi sportscar driver.

trajectory.title: Formula Monza debut
trajectory.description: Began his motorsport career in Formula Monza with a car he and his friends built, achieving little initial success.

trajectory.title: Italian Formula Three
trajectory.description: Competed in the Italian Formula Three championship, finishing as runner-up in his first season.

trajectory.title: European Formula Three Championship
trajectory.description: Won the European Formula Three Championship crown, paving the way for his entrance into Formula One.

trajectory.title: Formula One debut with Tyrrell
trajectory.description: Made his F1 debut at the 1981 San Marino Grand Prix with the Tyrrell team.

trajectory.title: First F1 victory at Las Vegas
trajectory.description: Won his first Formula One Grand Prix at the 1982 Caesars Palace Grand Prix in Las Vegas.

trajectory.title: Signed by Ferrari
trajectory.description: Joined Ferrari as the first Italian driver at the team since 1973, a calculated act of patriotic pride by Enzo Ferrari.

trajectory.title: F1 championship runner-up
trajectory.description: Finished second in the 1985 Formula One World Championship, the closest Ferrari came to a drivers' title between 1979 and 2000.

trajectory.title: 24 Hours of Le Mans winner
trajectory.description: Won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with Joest Racing in a Porsche-powered car.

trajectory.title: Death in testing crash
trajectory.description: Killed on April 25, 2001 while testing an Audi R8 at the Lausitzring in Germany, a month after winning the 12 Hours of Sebring.

name: Mo Yan
milestone_by_age_26: Published his first short story in a literary journal in 1981 at age 26, marking the beginning of his professional writing career while serving in the People's Liberation Army.
starting_point: Born Guan Moye in 1955 in Gaomi, Shandong Province, China to a peasant family; left school at age 12 during the Cultural Revolution to work in agriculture and later in a factory before joining the People's Liberation Army in 1976.
current_position: Continues writing and residing in Beijing, China; one of China's foremost contemporary authors.

trajectory.title: Joined the People's Liberation Army
trajectory.description: Enlisted in the PLA after multiple failed attempts, which provided the opportunity to study literature and begin writing.

trajectory.title: First published short story
trajectory.description: Published his first short story in a literary journal, marking the beginning of his professional writing career.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough with 'A Transparent Radish'
trajectory.description: Published the novella 'Touming de hong luobo' (A Transparent Radish), which brought him critical attention in Chinese literary circles.

trajectory.title: 'Red Sorghum' published
trajectory.description: Published the novel 'Hong gaoliang jiazu' (Red Sorghum), which was adapted into a Golden Bear-winning film by Zhang Yimou in 1988.

trajectory.title: 'The Republic of Wine'
trajectory.description: Published the satirical novel 'Jiuguo' (The Republic of Wine), judged subversive for its sharp criticism of contemporary Chinese society.

trajectory.title: 'Life and Death Are Wearing Me Out'
trajectory.description: Published 'Shengsi pilao' (Life and Death Are Wearing Me Out), using black humor to describe everyday life in the People's Republic.

trajectory.title: Nobel Prize in Literature
trajectory.description: Awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for work that 'with hallucinatory realism merges folk tales, history and the contemporary.'

trajectory.title: Continued literary career
trajectory.description: Continues to write and reside in Beijing as one of China's most internationally recognized authors.

name: Xavi
milestone_by_age_26: Made his first-team debut for FC Barcelona in August 1998 at age 18, scored on his official debut, and won the 1998-99 La Liga title at age 19, being named La Liga Breakthrough Player of the Year.
starting_point: Born in Terrassa, Barcelona, Catalonia in 1980; joined Barcelona's La Masia youth academy at age 11, with his father a former first-division player for Sabadell.
current_position: Former head coach of FC Barcelona (2021-2024); retired from playing in 2019 after a career at Barcelona, Al Sadd, and the Spanish national team.

trajectory.title: Joined La Masia
trajectory.description: Joined FC Barcelona's La Masia youth academy at age 11, beginning his lifelong association with the club.

trajectory.title: Barcelona first-team debut
trajectory.description: Made his first-team debut in August 1998 under Louis van Gaal, scoring on his official debut against Mallorca.

trajectory.title: La Liga title and Breakthrough Player
trajectory.description: Won the 1998-99 La Liga title and was named La Liga Breakthrough Player of the Year.

trajectory.title: Champions League winner
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Champions League with Barcelona, the club's second European Cup, establishing himself as a world-class midfielder.

trajectory.title: Euro 2008 champion
trajectory.description: Was instrumental in Spain's Euro 2008 victory, forming the midfield trio with Iniesta and Busquets that defined tiki-taka football.

trajectory.title: World Cup winner
trajectory.description: Won the 2010 FIFA World Cup with Spain, completing an unprecedented international treble (Euro 2008, World Cup 2010, Euro 2012).

trajectory.title: Second treble and departure from Barcelona
trajectory.description: Won his second continental treble with Barcelona before leaving for Al Sadd in Qatar, ending 17 years with the first team.

trajectory.title: Retirement from playing
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after four seasons with Al Sadd in Qatar.

trajectory.title: Barcelona head coach
trajectory.description: Returned to FC Barcelona as head coach in November 2021, managing the club until 2024.

name: Marita Koch
milestone_by_age_26: Set her first outdoor world record in the 400 metres in July 1978 at age 21, won two gold medals at the 1978 European Championships in Prague, and became the first woman to run 200 metres under 22 seconds in 1979 at age 22. By age 26 she had set multiple world records and won the 1983 World Championship 200m title.
starting_point: Born in Wismar, East Germany in 1957; displayed exceptional speed as a child, defeating older boys in sprint races, and began training under coach Wolfgang Meier at age 15, whom she later married.
current_position: Retired from competitive athletics since 1987; lives in Rostock, Germany with her husband and former coach Wolfgang Meier.

trajectory.title: First world record (indoor 400m)
trajectory.description: Set her first world record, running 400m indoors in 51.8 seconds in Milan.

trajectory.title: First outdoor world record and European Championship golds
trajectory.description: Set her first outdoor world record in the 400m (49.19 seconds) and won two gold medals at the European Championships in Prague.

trajectory.title: First woman under 22 seconds in 200m
trajectory.description: Became the first woman to run 200 metres under 22 seconds, setting a world record of 21.71 seconds that stood until 1988.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold in 400m
trajectory.description: Won Olympic gold in the 400m and silver in the 4x400m relay at the 1980 Moscow Olympics.

trajectory.title: World Championship dominance
trajectory.description: Was the most successful athlete at the inaugural World Athletics Championships in Helsinki, winning three golds and one silver medal.

trajectory.title: 400m world record (still standing)
trajectory.description: Set her final world record of 47.60 seconds in the 400m at the World Cup in Canberra, a record that still stands today.

trajectory.title: Retirement
trajectory.description: Retired from competitive athletics with 16 outdoor and 14 indoor world records to her name.

trajectory.title: International Track and Field Hall of Fame
trajectory.description: Inducted into the International Track and Field Hall of Fame as the first German woman, alongside Heike Drechsler.

name: Franco Baresi
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Serie A debut for AC Milan on April 23, 1978 at age 17, won the 1978-79 Serie A title in his first full season at 18, and was named club captain at age 22, becoming one of the youngest captains in Milan's history.
starting_point: Born in Travagliato, Italy in 1960; lost both parents by age 16; rejected by Inter Milan as too slight before joining AC Milan's youth system at age 14, while his older brother Giuseppe played for Inter.
current_position: Honorary Vice President of AC Milan since 2020; retired in 1997 after 20 years as a one-club player with AC Milan's No. 6 jersey retired in his honor.

trajectory.title: Serie A debut for AC Milan
trajectory.description: Made his Serie A debut for AC Milan, beginning a 20-year one-club career.

trajectory.title: Serie A title in first full season
trajectory.description: Won the 1978-79 Serie A title in his first full season with AC Milan.

trajectory.title: Named club captain
trajectory.description: Was named AC Milan captain at age 22, becoming one of the youngest captains in the club's history.

trajectory.title: FIFA World Cup winner
trajectory.description: Won the 1982 FIFA World Cup with Italy as a squad member, though he did not play in the tournament.

trajectory.title: European Cup winner
trajectory.description: Won the European Cup with AC Milan under Arrigo Sacchi, the first of three European Cups he would win.

trajectory.title: World Cup finalist and third European Cup
trajectory.description: Reached the 1994 World Cup final with Italy (missing the first penalty in the shootout) and won his third European Cup with AC Milan.

trajectory.title: Retirement and jersey retirement
trajectory.description: Retired after 20 years at AC Milan with 719 official matches; the club retired his No. 6 jersey in his honor.

trajectory.title: Honorary Vice President
trajectory.description: Appointed Honorary Vice President of AC Milan, continuing his 50-year association with the club.

name: Jean-Claude Van Damme
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Karate Championship as a member of the Belgian Karate Team on 26 December 1979 at age 19, and won the Mr. Belgium bodybuilding title in 1978 at age 17-18. Both are material competitive achievements before age 26, though his acting breakthrough came later with Bloodsport (1988) at age 28.
starting_point: Born in Berchem-Sainte-Agathe, Brussels, Belgium in 1960 to an accountant father; enrolled in Shotokan karate at age 10 by his father and earned a black belt at 18, also studying ballet for five years.
current_position: Continues acting in films; resides in Los Angeles, California, known as 'The Muscles from Brussels.'

trajectory.title: Began martial arts fight career
trajectory.description: Started his competitive martial arts career, eventually posting a 41-4 semi-contact karate record and 18-1 kickboxing record.

trajectory.title: Mr. Belgium bodybuilding title
trajectory.description: Won the Mr. Belgium bodybuilding title while also training in martial arts and ballet.

trajectory.title: European Karate Championship
trajectory.description: Won the European Professional Karate Association middleweight championship as a member of the Belgian Karate Team.

trajectory.title: Moved to Los Angeles
trajectory.description: Moved to the United States to pursue an acting career, working as a bouncer, carpet layer, and aerobics instructor while seeking roles.

trajectory.title: First named acting role
trajectory.description: Got his first named acting role as the villain Ivan Kraschinsky in 'No Retreat, No Surrender.'

trajectory.title: Breakthrough with 'Bloodsport'
trajectory.description: Starred in 'Bloodsport,' which grossed $35 million at the box office and launched his action film career.

trajectory.title: 'Timecop' box office success
trajectory.description: Starred in 'Timecop,' his most commercially successful film, cementing his status as a major action star.

trajectory.title: Critical acclaim with 'JCVD'
trajectory.description: Received critical acclaim for his dramatic performance in the meta-film 'JCVD,' showcasing range beyond action roles.

name: Linda Evangelista
milestone_by_age_26: Signed with Elite Model Management and had her first major fashion magazine cover (L'Officiel, November 1984) at age 19. By age 26 (1991), she was one of the most famous supermodels in the world, featured on the cover of British Vogue (January 1990) and in George Michael's 'Freedom! '90' video.
starting_point: Born in St. Catharines, Ontario, Canada in 1965 to Italian immigrant working-class parents; her father worked for General Motors and her mother was a bookkeeper; enrolled in modeling school at age 12.
current_position: Continues to model sporadically; lives in the United States; publicly disclosed a disfiguring cosmetic procedure experience in 2021.

trajectory.title: Spotted at Miss Teen Niagara
trajectory.description: Was noticed by a talent agent from Elite Model Management at the Miss Teen Niagara beauty pageant, though she did not win.

trajectory.title: Signed with Elite and first major cover
trajectory.description: Signed with Elite Model Management, moved to Paris, and appeared on her first major fashion magazine cover (L'Officiel, November 1984).

trajectory.title: Versace campaign and Vogue cover
trajectory.description: Appeared in Versace advertising campaigns and on the cover of French Vogue, establishing herself in high fashion.

trajectory.title: Iconic short haircut
trajectory.description: Had her hair cut short at the suggestion of photographer Peter Lindbergh, a look that became iconic and revolutionized model styling.

trajectory.title: 'Freedom! '90' video and supermodel era
trajectory.description: Appeared in George Michael's 'Freedom! '90' music video alongside other supermodels, cementing her status as one of the 'Big 6' supermodels.

trajectory.title: Retirement from modeling
trajectory.description: Retired from her full-time modeling career, making a sporadic comeback three years later.

trajectory.title: Greatest Supermodel of All Time
trajectory.description: Voted 'The Greatest Supermodel of All Time' by viewers of the television show Fashion File.

trajectory.title: Public disclosure of cosmetic procedure injury
trajectory.description: Publicly revealed she had been 'brutally disfigured' by a Zeltiq CoolSculpting procedure, spending five years in hiding before speaking out.

name: John Lydon
milestone_by_age_26: Became lead vocalist of the Sex Pistols in 1975 at age 19. The band released 'Anarchy in the U.K.' (November 1976), 'God Save the Queen' (May 1977), and the album 'Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols' (28 October 1977) at age 21. He then founded Public Image Ltd in 1978 at age 22, releasing their debut album in 1978.
starting_point: Born in Finsbury Park, London in 1956 to Irish working-class parents; contracted spinal meningitis at age seven, which erased most of his early memories and left minor lasting effects; grew up in a council flat sharing an outdoor toilet with neighbors.
current_position: Continues to perform and make public appearances; resides in the United States; last active with Public Image Ltd which reformed in 2009.

trajectory.title: Joined Sex Pistols as lead vocalist
trajectory.description: Was spotted wearing an 'I Hate Pink Floyd' T-shirt and invited to audition for the Sex Pistols, becoming 'Johnny Rotten.'

trajectory.title: 'Anarchy in the U.K.' released
trajectory.description: The Sex Pistols released their debut single 'Anarchy in the U.K.' in November 1976, defining the punk rock movement.

trajectory.title: 'Never Mind the Bollocks' album
trajectory.description: The Sex Pistols released their only studio album 'Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols' on October 28, 1977, one of the most influential punk albums ever.

trajectory.title: Founded Public Image Ltd
trajectory.description: After the Sex Pistols disbanded in January 1978, founded Public Image Ltd (PiL), a far more experimental post-punk band.

trajectory.title: PiL debut album 'First Issue'
trajectory.description: Released PiL's debut album 'First Issue,' establishing a new musical direction described as 'arguably the first post-rock group.'

trajectory.title: PiL album 'Album' and collaborations
trajectory.description: Released the PiL album 'Album' featuring collaborations with artists like Ryuichi Sakamoto and Steve Vai.

trajectory.title: 'Open Up' with Leftfield
trajectory.description: Collaborated with dance duo Leftfield on the pioneering single 'Open Up,' a crossover hit.

trajectory.title: PiL reformation
trajectory.description: Reformed Public Image Ltd after a 17-year hiatus, continuing to tour and release new music.

name: Zlatan Ibrahimovic
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Ajax in July 2001 at age 19-20 and won the 2001-02 Eredivisie title. By age 26 (October 2007), he had also played for Juventus (2004-2006) and Inter Milan (2006-2007), won multiple league titles, been named Serie A Foreign Footballer of the Year (2005), and won the Guldbollen (Swedish player of the year) in 2005.
starting_point: Born in Malmo, Sweden in 1981 to a Bosnian-Croatian father and Croatian mother; grew up in the immigrant-heavy Rosengard district, beginning his football career with local club Malmo FF's youth team.
current_position: Retired from professional football in 2023 at age 41; last played for AC Milan; involved in football management and business ventures.

trajectory.title: Malmo FF senior debut
trajectory.description: Began his professional career at Malmo FF in the Swedish Allsvenskan.

trajectory.title: Signed for Ajax
trajectory.description: Joined Ajax in July 2001 and won the 2001-02 Eredivisie title, gaining a reputation as one of Europe's most promising forwards.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Juventus
trajectory.description: Signed for Juventus, where he won Serie A titles (later revoked due to Calciopoli scandal) and was named Serie A Foreign Footballer of the Year in 2005.

trajectory.title: Move to Inter Milan
trajectory.description: Joined Inter Milan after Juventus were relegated, winning three consecutive Serie A titles and establishing himself as a world-class striker.

trajectory.title: Record transfer to Barcelona
trajectory.description: Moved to Barcelona in one of the world's most expensive transfers, though his stint lasted only one season.

trajectory.title: PSG dominance begins
trajectory.description: Joined Paris Saint-Germain, leading them to their first Ligue 1 title in 19 years and becoming the club's all-time leading goalscorer.

trajectory.title: Manchester United and Europa League
trajectory.description: Joined Manchester United on a free transfer, winning the EFL Cup and UEFA Europa League in his first season.

trajectory.title: Retirement from AC Milan
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football in 2023 after a second stint at AC Milan, having won 34 trophies and scored over 570 career goals.

name: Michèle Mouton
milestone_by_age_26: Crowned French and European ladies' rally champion in 1974 at age 23, then won the two-litre prototype class at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1975 at age 24, and was signed by Fiat France for 1977 finishing runner-up in the European Rally Championship at age 25-26.
starting_point: Born in Grasse, France in 1951; began rallying as a co-driver before switching to the driver's seat, with her father Pierre buying her an Alpine A110 on the condition she prove herself.
current_position: Retired from competitive rallying since 1986; co-founded the Race of Champions event and served as first president of the FIA's Women in Motorsport Commission from 2010.

trajectory.title: Rally debut as co-driver
trajectory.description: Began her rallying career as a co-driver at the Monte Carlo Rally before quickly moving to the driver's seat.

trajectory.title: French and European ladies' rally champion
trajectory.description: Crowned French and European ladies' rally champion, driving an Alpine-Renault A110.

trajectory.title: Le Mans class winner
trajectory.description: Won the two-litre prototype class at the 24 Hours of Le Mans as part of an all-female crew in a Moynet LM75.

trajectory.title: Signed by Fiat France
trajectory.description: Signed by Fiat France as a works driver, finishing runner-up in the European Rally Championship.

trajectory.title: First WRC win by a woman
trajectory.description: Won the Rallye Sanremo, becoming the first woman to win a round of the FIA World Rally Championship.

trajectory.title: WRC championship runner-up
trajectory.description: Finished second overall in the 1982 World Rally Championship with wins in Portugal, Brazil, and Greece, helping Audi to its first manufacturers' title.

trajectory.title: Pikes Peak record
trajectory.description: Won the Pikes Peak International Hill Climb in the United States, setting a record time in the process.

trajectory.title: German Rally Championship and retirement
trajectory.description: Won the German Rally Championship with Peugeot, becoming the first female driver to win a major championship in rallying, before retiring due to the Group B ban.

trajectory.title: FIA Women in Motorsport Commission president
trajectory.description: Became the first president of the FIA's Women in Motorsport Commission, advocating for women in the sport.

name: Kimi Räikkönen
milestone_by_age_26: Made Formula One debut with Sauber in 2001 at age 21, achieved maiden podium on debut with McLaren in 2002, won first Grand Prix at Malaysia in 2003 at age 23, and won seven Grands Prix finishing runner-up to Fernando Alonso in the 2005 championship at age 26.
starting_point: Born in Espoo, Finland in 1979; began competitive kart racing at age 10, winning national titles before graduating to junior formulae in 1999 with only 23 car races before his F1 debut.
current_position: Retired from Formula One in 2021 after 19 seasons; lives in Switzerland, known as 'the Iceman.'

trajectory.title: British Formula Renault champion
trajectory.description: Dominated the British Formula Renault Championship with Manor Motorsport, prompting Sauber to sign him for Formula One.

trajectory.title: Formula One debut with Sauber
trajectory.description: Made his F1 debut with Sauber despite having only 23 car races to his name, scoring points on his debut in Australia.

trajectory.title: Joined McLaren and maiden podium
trajectory.description: Replaced Mika Hakkinen at McLaren, achieving his maiden F1 podium on debut at the Australian Grand Prix.

trajectory.title: First Grand Prix win
trajectory.description: Won his first Formula One Grand Prix at Malaysia, finishing runner-up to Michael Schumacher in the championship by just two points.

trajectory.title: Championship runner-up with seven wins
trajectory.description: Won seven Grands Prix but finished runner-up to Fernando Alonso in the 2005 championship due to reliability issues.

trajectory.title: Formula One World Champion
trajectory.description: Won the Formula One World Drivers' Championship with Ferrari, beating Alonso and Hamilton by a single point.

trajectory.title: Return to F1 with Lotus
trajectory.description: Returned to Formula One after a two-year sabbatical in rallying, scoring Lotus's only victories at Abu Dhabi and Australia.

trajectory.title: Final F1 win at US Grand Prix
trajectory.description: Won his final Formula One Grand Prix at the 2018 United States Grand Prix with Ferrari, 113 races after his previous win.

trajectory.title: Retirement from Formula One
trajectory.description: Retired from Formula One after 19 seasons and 349 race starts, leaving as one of the sport's most beloved characters.

name: Johnny Depp
milestone_by_age_26: Became a teen idol starring as Officer Tom Hanson in the Fox television series '21 Jump Street', which premiered in 1987 when Depp was 24; had already made his feature film debut in 'A Nightmare on Elm Street' (1984) at age 21 and appeared in 'Platoon' (1986).
starting_point: Born in Owensboro, Kentucky in 1963; youngest of four children to a waitress mother and civil engineer father; family moved frequently before settling in Miramar, Florida in 1970; parents divorced when he was 15.
current_position: Continues acting in films; resides in the United States; re-established his career after a highly publicized defamation trial in 2022.

trajectory.title: Feature film debut in 'A Nightmare on Elm Street'
trajectory.description: Made his film debut in Wes Craven's horror classic after being introduced to acting by Nicolas Cage.

trajectory.title: Appeared in 'Platoon'
trajectory.description: Had a supporting role in Oliver Stone's Academy Award-winning Vietnam War film 'Platoon.'

trajectory.title: '21 Jump Street' teen idol
trajectory.description: Became a teen idol starring as Officer Tom Hanson in the Fox television series '21 Jump Street,' which premiered in 1987.

trajectory.title: 'Edward Scissorhands' and Tim Burton collaboration
trajectory.description: Starred in 'Edward Scissorhands,' his first collaboration with director Tim Burton, marking his transition to film star.

trajectory.title: Captain Jack Sparrow in 'Pirates of the Caribbean'
trajectory.description: Portrayed Captain Jack Sparrow in 'Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl,' receiving an Academy Award nomination and launching a blockbuster franchise.

trajectory.title: World's highest-paid actor
trajectory.description: Listed by Guinness World Records as the world's highest-paid actor with earnings of $75 million.

trajectory.title: Defamation trial and career resurgence
trajectory.description: Won a high-profile defamation trial against ex-wife Amber Heard, leading to a career resurgence including a directing role and new film projects.

name: Sia
milestone_by_age_26: Her debut solo single 'Taken for Granted' peaked at #10 on the UK Singles Chart in June 2000 at age 24, also topping the UK R&B Chart; her second studio album 'Healing Is Difficult' was released in 2001 at age 25, establishing her as a recording artist in the UK market.
starting_point: Born Sia Kate Isobelle Furler in Adelaide, Australia in 1975; raised in an artistic household by a musician father and art lecturer mother; started her career singing in the local acid jazz band Crisp in the mid-1990s.
current_position: Continues songwriting and releasing music; resides in the United States; one of pop music's most in-demand songwriters.

trajectory.title: Debut solo album 'OnlySee'
trajectory.description: Released her debut studio album 'OnlySee' in Australia after Crisp disbanded; the album sold about 1,200 copies.

trajectory.title: 'Taken for Granted' UK Top 10
trajectory.description: Her debut solo single 'Taken for Granted' peaked at #10 on the UK Singles Chart and topped the UK R&B Chart.

trajectory.title: 'Healing Is Difficult' album
trajectory.description: Released her second studio album 'Healing Is Difficult,' establishing her as a recording artist in the UK market.

trajectory.title: 'Colour the Small One' and 'Breathe Me'
trajectory.description: Released third album featuring 'Breathe Me,' which gained widespread recognition when used in the finale of TV show 'Six Feet Under.'

trajectory.title: Songwriting breakthrough
trajectory.description: Achieved massive success as a songwriter with 'Titanium' (with David Guetta) and 'Wild Ones' (with Flo Rida), both top-ten hits.

trajectory.title: 'Chandelier' and mainstream solo breakthrough
trajectory.description: Released '1000 Forms of Fear' featuring the Grammy-nominated single 'Chandelier,' which became a global hit and her signature song.

trajectory.title: 'Cheap Thrills' Billboard #1
trajectory.description: 'Cheap Thrills' from the album 'This Is Acting' became her first single to top the Billboard Hot 100 chart.

trajectory.title: Directorial debut with 'Music'
trajectory.description: Directed and co-wrote the musical film 'Music,' expanding her creative output beyond songwriting and performing.

name: Richard Clayderman
milestone_by_age_26: Recorded 'Ballade pour Adeline' in 1976 at age 23, which became a massive international hit selling millions of copies and launching a career that has sold over 120 million records worldwide.
starting_point: Born Philippe Pages in Paris in 1953; learned piano from his father, a piano teacher; accepted into the Paris Conservatory of Music at age 12 and won first prize at 16 before financial difficulties from his father's illness forced him to work as a session musician.
current_position: Continues touring internationally as a concert pianist; certified by Guinness World Records as 'the most successful pianist in the world.'

trajectory.title: Accepted into Paris Conservatory
trajectory.description: Was accepted into the Conservatoire de Paris at age 12, where he would win first prize in a piano competition at 16.

trajectory.title: Recorded 'Ballade pour Adeline'
trajectory.description: Recorded 'Ballade pour Adeline' at the urging of producers Olivier Toussaint and Paul de Senneville, which became a massive international hit selling over 20 million copies.

trajectory.title: International breakthrough
trajectory.description: 'Ballade pour Adeline' was distributed in 38 countries, launching his career as an international recording artist.

trajectory.title: Carnegie Hall concert
trajectory.description: Performed at Carnegie Hall in New York, expanding his international concert career.

trajectory.title: 800 million viewer Chinese TV broadcast
trajectory.description: A live concert broadcast on Chinese television attracted over 800 million viewers, establishing his enormous popularity in Asia.

trajectory.title: Guinness World Record
trajectory.description: Certified by the Guinness Book of World Records as 'the most successful pianist in the world,' having sold over 120 million records.

trajectory.title: Continued touring
trajectory.description: Continues to tour internationally, particularly popular in Japan and Asia, maintaining an active concert schedule.

name: Aki Kaurismäki
milestone_by_age_26: Directed his debut feature film Crime and Punishment (1983), an adaptation of Dostoevsky set in modern Helsinki, at age 26, having co-founded the production company Villealfa Filmproductions with his brother Mika.
starting_point: Born in Orimattila, Finland in 1957; graduated with a degree in media studies from the University of Tampere; worked as a bricklayer, dishwasher, and postman before entering film as a critic and collaborator with his brother Mika.
current_position: Continues filmmaking; lives in Lisbon, Portugal since 1989; Finland's most famous film director.

trajectory.title: Film debut and Villealfa founded
trajectory.description: Made his film debut as co-screenwriter and lead actor in brother Mika's 'The Liar' and co-founded Villealfa Filmproductions.

trajectory.title: Directorial debut with 'Crime and Punishment'
trajectory.description: Directed his debut feature film 'Crime and Punishment,' an adaptation of Dostoevsky set in modern Helsinki.

trajectory.title: 'Shadows in Paradise'
trajectory.description: Released 'Shadows in Paradise,' part of his 'Proletariat Trilogy' and a key work in his distinctive minimalist style.

trajectory.title: 'Leningrad Cowboys Go America'
trajectory.description: Gained worldwide attention with 'Leningrad Cowboys Go America,' a cult hit that expanded his international reputation.

trajectory.title: 'Drifting Clouds'
trajectory.description: Released 'Drifting Clouds,' a critically acclaimed film about unemployment and resilience in Finland.

trajectory.title: Grand Prix at Cannes for 'The Man Without a Past'
trajectory.description: Won the Grand Prix at the Cannes Film Festival for 'The Man Without a Past,' his most successful film.

trajectory.title: 'Le Havre' acclaim
trajectory.description: Released 'Le Havre,' which premiered at Cannes and received widespread critical acclaim for its humanitarian themes.

trajectory.title: 'Fallen Leaves' and Cannes Jury Prize
trajectory.description: Released 'Fallen Leaves,' which won the Jury Prize at the 2023 Cannes Film Festival, continuing his acclaimed career.

name: Sinéad O'Connor
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut album The Lion and the Cobra in October 1987 at age 20, achieving international chart success and a Grammy nomination, followed by the seven-million-selling I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got in 1990 at age 23.
starting_point: Born in Dublin, Ireland in 1966; had a difficult childhood with an abusive mother; was sent to a Magdalene laundry reform school at 14 where a nun gave her a guitar and set her up with a music teacher, launching her musical career.
current_position: Died on July 26, 2023 at age 56 in London, England; final role as an influential Irish singer-songwriter and activist.

trajectory.title: Discovered and first recordings
trajectory.description: Was discovered by the drummer of Irish band In Tua Nua and co-wrote their hit 'Take My Hand' before signing with Ensign Records.

trajectory.title: Debut album 'The Lion and the Cobra'
trajectory.description: Released debut album 'The Lion and the Cobra' in October 1987, achieving international chart success and a Grammy nomination.

trajectory.title: 'I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got' and 'Nothing Compares 2 U'
trajectory.description: Released the seven-million-selling album featuring 'Nothing Compares 2 U,' which topped charts worldwide and became her signature song.

trajectory.title: Grammy Award
trajectory.description: Won the Grammy Award for Best Alternative Album for 'I Do Not Want What I Haven't Got' and was named artist of the year by Rolling Stone.

trajectory.title: SNL pope photo controversy
trajectory.description: Tore up a photograph of Pope John Paul II on Saturday Night Live, a protest against Catholic Church sexual abuse that sparked global controversy.

trajectory.title: Final studio album 'I'm Not Bossy, I'm The Boss'
trajectory.description: Released her tenth and final studio album, returning to impassioned pop after years of exploring various musical styles.

trajectory.title: Conversion to Islam
trajectory.description: Converted to Islam and adopted the name Shuhada' Sadaqat, while continuing to perform under her birth name.

trajectory.title: Death
trajectory.description: Died on July 26, 2023 in London; posthumously nominated for induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2024.

name: David Hasselhoff
milestone_by_age_26: Landed a regular leading role as Dr. Snapper Foster on the CBS soap opera The Young and the Restless in December 1975, which he held for six years.
starting_point: Born in Baltimore, Maryland in 1952; began acting at age seven in Peter Pan; studied theater at the California Institute of the Arts until 1973 before landing his first television role.
current_position: Continues acting and performing; holds a Guinness World Record as the most watched man on TV; resides in the United States.

trajectory.title: Early acting career
trajectory.description: Studied theater at the California Institute of the Arts and began pursuing acting roles in Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: 'The Young and the Restless' breakthrough
trajectory.description: Landed the regular leading role of Dr. Snapper Foster on the CBS soap opera 'The Young and the Restless,' which he held for six years.

trajectory.title: 'Knight Rider' leading role
trajectory.description: Starred as Michael Knight in NBC's hit series 'Knight Rider,' which became a huge success in the US and overseas and earned him a People's Choice Award.

trajectory.title: 'Baywatch' launched
trajectory.description: Returned to television to produce and star in 'Baywatch' as Mitch Buchannon, which became the most watched show in TV history.

trajectory.title: Baywatch global phenomenon
trajectory.description: 'Baywatch' reached its peak global popularity, airing in 148 countries and making Hasselhoff one of the most recognizable faces on television worldwide.

trajectory.title: 'America's Got Talent' judge
trajectory.description: Served as a judge on the first season of 'America's Got Talent,' expanding his television career into reality TV.

trajectory.title: 'Baywatch' film cameo
trajectory.description: Made a cameo appearance in the 'Baywatch' feature film reboot, cementing his cultural association with the franchise.

name: Rivaldo
milestone_by_age_26: Signed for FC Barcelona in 1997 at age 25 as a 17 million pound replacement for Ronaldo, going on to win consecutive La Liga titles in 1998 and 1999.
starting_point: Born in Recife, Brazil in 1972; grew up in a favela where he sold chewing gum and ice lollies on the streets; received his first football boots from his father at age 13 and joined Santa Cruz's youth setup at 16.
current_position: Retired from professional football in 2013; involved in football business and management in Brazil.

trajectory.title: Professional debut with Santa Cruz
trajectory.description: Began his professional career with Santa Cruz in Brazil after a successful trial, later moving to Mogi Mirim and Corinthians.

trajectory.title: Brazilian championship with Palmeiras
trajectory.description: Won the Brazilian national championship with Palmeiras, establishing himself as a top domestic player.

trajectory.title: Move to Europe with Deportivo La Coruna
trajectory.description: Moved to Spanish side Deportivo La Coruna, scoring 20 goals in a 16-game stretch and earning a transfer to Barcelona.

trajectory.title: Signed for FC Barcelona
trajectory.description: Signed for Barcelona as a 17 million pound replacement for Ronaldo, scoring twice on his league debut and winning La Liga and Copa del Rey in his first season.

trajectory.title: Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player
trajectory.description: Won the Ballon d'Or and was named FIFA World Player of the Year after winning a second consecutive La Liga title with Barcelona.

trajectory.title: Iconic bicycle kick hat-trick vs Valencia
trajectory.description: Scored a last-minute bicycle kick to complete a hat-trick against Valencia, qualifying Barcelona for the Champions League and widely ranked as the greatest hat-trick ever.

trajectory.title: FIFA World Cup winner with Brazil
trajectory.description: Won the 2002 FIFA World Cup with Brazil as part of the fearsome Ronaldo-Ronaldinho-Rivaldo frontline.

trajectory.title: Champions League winner with AC Milan
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Champions League with AC Milan, completing a career triple of World Cup, Champions League, and Ballon d'Or.

name: Francesco Totti
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest club captain in Serie A history at age 22 in October 1998, and was named Serie A Young Footballer of the Year for the 1998-99 season, having made his Serie A debut at 16 in March 1993.
starting_point: Born in Rome in 1976; joined Roma's youth academy in 1989 at age 13 after his mother refused lucrative offers from Milan to keep him in his hometown; idolized former Roma captain Giuseppe Giannini.
current_position: Retired from professional football in 2017 after 25 seasons at AS Roma; involved in football management and Roma club ambassador roles.

trajectory.title: Serie A debut for Roma
trajectory.description: Made his Serie A debut for Roma on March 28, 1993 at age 16, coming off the bench in a 2-0 win over Brescia.

trajectory.title: First Serie A goal
trajectory.description: Scored his first Serie A goal on September 4, 1994 in a 1-1 draw against Foggia.

trajectory.title: Youngest Serie A captain
trajectory.description: Became the youngest club captain in Serie A history at age 22 in October 1998, taking the armband from Aldair.

trajectory.title: Serie A Young Footballer of the Year
trajectory.description: Named Serie A Young Footballer of the Year for the 1998-99 season, cementing his status as a rising star.

trajectory.title: Serie A title with Roma
trajectory.description: Won his first and only Serie A title with Roma, scoring in the 3-1 win over Parma on the final day that clinched the championship.

trajectory.title: FIFA World Cup winner with Italy
trajectory.description: Played all seven games as Italy won the 2006 FIFA World Cup, scoring once and providing three assists.

trajectory.title: European Golden Shoe
trajectory.description: Won the Serie A golden boot and European Golden Shoe with 26 league goals, his best single-season tally of 32 goals in all competitions.

trajectory.title: Retirement after 25 seasons at Roma
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after 25 seasons at AS Roma, having made 786 appearances and scored 307 goals for his only club.

name: Uli Hoeneß
milestone_by_age_26: Won three consecutive Bundesliga titles (1972-1974), three consecutive European Cups (1974-1976), the 1972 European Championship, and the 1974 FIFA World Cup with West Germany, all by age 24; scored twice in the 1974 European Cup final replay.
starting_point: Born in Ulm, West Germany in 1952 to a master butcher father; began playing football at VfB Ulm's youth department before joining Bayern Munich at 18 under coach Udo Lattek.
current_position: Honorary President of Bayern Munich; previously served as general manager (1979-2009) and president (2009-2014, 2016-2019) of the club.

trajectory.title: Joined Bayern Munich
trajectory.description: Moved from TSG Ulm 1846 to Bayern Munich, immediately impressing coach Udo Lattek and earning a regular spot.

trajectory.title: First DFB-Pokal title
trajectory.description: Won his first major honour with the 1971 DFB-Pokal, scoring in the final against Koln.

trajectory.title: Bundesliga title and European Championship
trajectory.description: Won the first of three consecutive Bundesliga titles with Bayern and the 1972 European Championship with West Germany.

trajectory.title: World Cup and European Cup double
trajectory.description: Won the 1974 FIFA World Cup with West Germany and the European Cup with Bayern, scoring twice in the European Cup final replay against Atletico Madrid.

trajectory.title: Third consecutive European Cup
trajectory.description: Won his third consecutive European Cup with Bayern Munich, completing a historic hat-trick of European titles.

trajectory.title: Retirement and Bayern general manager
trajectory.description: Retired from playing at 27 due to injury and became Bayern Munich's general manager, a role he held for 30 years.

trajectory.title: Bayern Munich president
trajectory.description: Became president of Bayern Munich after 30 years as general manager, during which he built the club into a global brand.

trajectory.title: Tax evasion conviction
trajectory.description: Pleaded guilty to tax evasion and served 18 months in prison, before returning to Bayern Munich's presidency in 2016.

name: Mario Kempes
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1978 FIFA World Cup with Argentina at age 24, finishing as the tournament's top scorer (6 goals) and best player (Golden Ball), after becoming top scorer in the Argentine championship at age 20 and La Liga top scorer at age 22-23.
starting_point: Born in Bell Ville, Argentina in 1954, a town known as 'the national capital of football'; began his youth career with local clubs before joining Instituto, where he scored 11 goals in 13 games as a teenager.
current_position: Retired from professional football in 1996; works as a football commentator and analyst for ESPN Deportes.

trajectory.title: Professional debut with Instituto
trajectory.description: Began his professional career with Instituto, scoring 11 goals in 13 games before transferring to Rosario Central.

trajectory.title: Top scorer at Rosario Central
trajectory.description: Became a prolific scorer at Rosario Central, scoring 85 goals in three seasons and earning his first Argentina national team call-up.

trajectory.title: Move to Valencia and La Liga top scorer
trajectory.description: Transferred to Valencia in Spain, becoming La Liga's top scorer with 24 goals in his first season.

trajectory.title: World Cup winner, Golden Boot and Golden Ball
trajectory.description: Won the 1978 FIFA World Cup with Argentina, scoring twice in the final and winning both the Golden Boot (top scorer) and Golden Ball (best player).

trajectory.title: South American Footballer of the Year
trajectory.description: Named South American Footballer of the Year and Onze d'Or European Footballer of the Year after his World Cup heroics.

trajectory.title: River Plate and Argentine title
trajectory.description: Returned to Argentina to play for River Plate, winning the Argentine Metropolitano championship.

trajectory.title: Return to Valencia
trajectory.description: Returned to Valencia for two more seasons before moving to Hercules and later lower-division Austrian clubs.

trajectory.title: FIFA 100 list
trajectory.description: Named by Pele as one of the 125 greatest living footballers as part of FIFA's 100th anniversary celebration.

name: Raúl
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for Real Madrid's first team at age 17 in October 1994, won La Liga that season, and by age 26 had won three Champions League titles (1998, 2000, 2002), six La Liga titles, and become one of the world's greatest strikers.
starting_point: Born in Madrid in 1977 in the suburb of San Cristobal de los Angeles; initially played for Atletico Madrid's youth academy before signing with Real Madrid's youth teams in 1992.
current_position: Retired from professional football in 2015; currently manages Real Madrid Castilla (Real Madrid's reserve team).

trajectory.title: Joined Real Madrid youth from Atletico
trajectory.description: Signed with Real Madrid's youth teams after being released by Atletico Madrid's academy, scoring 13 goals in 7 games.

trajectory.title: Real Madrid first-team debut
trajectory.description: Made his first-team debut on October 29, 1994 under Jorge Valdano, and won La Liga in his debut season.

trajectory.title: First Champions League title
trajectory.description: Won Real Madrid's seventh European Cup, beating Juventus in the final, beginning a dynasty of European success.

trajectory.title: Second Champions League and scored in final
trajectory.description: Won his second Champions League title, scoring in the final against Valencia, and became one of the world's highest-rated strikers.

trajectory.title: Ballon d'Or runner-up
trajectory.description: Finished as runner-up for the Ballon d'Or, establishing himself as one of the world's premier forwards.

trajectory.title: Third Champions League and Real Madrid captain
trajectory.description: Won his third Champions League title (scoring in the final again) and became captain of Real Madrid.

trajectory.title: Departure from Real Madrid
trajectory.description: Left Real Madrid after 16 years with 323 goals in 741 appearances, signing for Schalke 04 in the Bundesliga.

trajectory.title: Retirement after New York Cosmos stint
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after spells at Schalke 04, Al Sadd, and the New York Cosmos, with over 1,000 career appearances.

trajectory.title: Real Madrid Castilla manager
trajectory.description: Became manager of Real Madrid Castilla, the club's reserve team, beginning his coaching career.

name: Jacques Villeneuve
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Indianapolis 500 and the IndyCar World Series championship in 1995 at age 24, becoming the youngest IndyCar champion and first Canadian Indy 500 winner; then won the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 1997 at age 26.
starting_point: Born in Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu, Quebec, Canada in 1971; son of Ferrari F1 driver Gilles Villeneuve, who was killed in a racing accident in 1982; raised in Monaco and attended boarding school in Switzerland before beginning racing at 17.
current_position: Retired from competitive racing; involved in motorsport commentary and various business ventures; resides in Monaco.

trajectory.title: Began racing in Italian Formula Three
trajectory.description: Began his racing career at age 17 under an Andorran license, progressing to Italian Formula Three.

trajectory.title: Toyota Atlantic Championship
trajectory.description: Finished third overall in the Toyota Atlantic Championship with five wins in 15 races, gaining attention from IndyCar teams.

trajectory.title: IndyCar debut and Rookie of the Year
trajectory.description: Debuted in CART IndyCar with Forsythe/Green Racing, finishing sixth in the championship with one victory and earning Rookie of the Year.

trajectory.title: Indy 500 and IndyCar champion
trajectory.description: Won the Indianapolis 500 and the IndyCar World Series championship, becoming the youngest IndyCar champion and first Canadian Indy 500 winner.

trajectory.title: Formula One debut with Williams
trajectory.description: Moved to Formula One with Williams, winning four Grands Prix and finishing as championship runner-up to teammate Damon Hill as a rookie.

trajectory.title: Formula One World Champion
trajectory.description: Won the Formula One World Drivers' Championship with Williams, beating Michael Schumacher in a controversial season finale.

trajectory.title: Departure from Formula One
trajectory.description: Left Formula One after 11 seasons, having won 11 Grands Prix and the 1997 world championship.

trajectory.title: Post-racing career
trajectory.description: Involved in motorsport commentary and various racing-related business ventures after retiring from competitive driving.

name: Ole Einar Bjørndalen
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Overall Biathlon World Cup title in 1997-98 at age 24, Olympic gold in the 10km sprint at the 1998 Nagano Olympics, and a World Championship gold medal — achieving all three major biathlon titles in one season.
starting_point: Born in Drammen, Norway in 1974; the youngest of five children on a farm in Simostranda; followed his older brother Dag into biathlon and left home at 16 to attend a sports academy in Geilo to focus on the sport.
current_position: Retired from competitive biathlon in 2018 at age 44; involved in biathlon coaching and sports administration.

trajectory.title: Junior World Championship and World Cup debut
trajectory.description: Won three junior world championship titles and made his Biathlon World Cup debut, an unprecedented junior medal haul.

trajectory.title: Olympic debut at Lillehammer
trajectory.description: Competed at the 1994 Winter Olympics in his home country of Norway, with a best individual finish of 28th in the sprint.

trajectory.title: First World Cup victory
trajectory.description: Obtained his first major World Cup victory on January 11, 1996 in an individual competition in Antholz-Anterselva, Italy.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold and Overall World Cup title
trajectory.description: Won Olympic gold in the 10km sprint at Nagano and the Overall Biathlon World Cup title, achieving all three major biathlon titles in one season.

trajectory.title: Four Olympic golds at Salt Lake City
trajectory.description: Swept all four biathlon gold medals at the 2002 Winter Olympics, the first biathlete to win four golds at a single Games.

trajectory.title: Sixth Overall World Cup title
trajectory.description: Won his fourth Overall World Cup title, adding to his dominance of the sport across multiple seasons.

trajectory.title: Two more Olympic golds at Sochi
trajectory.description: Won two more Olympic gold medals at Sochi at age 40, bringing his career total to 13 Olympic medals, the most for any male Winter Olympian.

trajectory.title: Retirement as 'King of Biathlon'
trajectory.description: Retired at age 44 with 95 World Cup wins, six Overall World Cup titles, and 45 World Championship medals, widely considered the greatest biathlete of all time.

name: Oliver Kahn
milestone_by_age_26: Transferred to Bayern Munich in 1994 at age 25 for a record goalkeeper fee of DM 4.6 million, becoming the club's starting goalkeeper, after establishing himself at Karlsruher SC and reaching the 1993-94 UEFA Cup semi-finals.
starting_point: Born in Karlsruhe, West Germany in 1969; joined Karlsruher SC at age six where his father had played, starting as a field player before becoming a goalkeeper.
current_position: Former CEO of Bayern Munich (2021-2023); retired from professional football in 2008; involved in football business and commentary.

trajectory.title: Karlsruher SC professional debut
trajectory.description: Made his debut in Karlsruher SC's professional squad in the 1987-88 Bundesliga season, initially as reserve goalkeeper.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Bayern Munich
trajectory.description: Transferred to Bayern Munich for a record goalkeeper fee of DM 4.6 million, becoming the club's starting goalkeeper.

trajectory.title: UEFA Cup winner with Bayern
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Cup with Bayern Munich, his first major European trophy.

trajectory.title: European Championship winner with Germany
trajectory.description: Won the 1996 UEFA European Championship with Germany, though he was the backup goalkeeper.

trajectory.title: Champions League and Intercontinental Cup
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Champions League and Intercontinental Cup with Bayern Munich, cementing his status as one of the world's best goalkeepers.

trajectory.title: World Cup runner-up and Golden Ball
trajectory.description: Led Germany to the 2002 World Cup final as captain, winning the tournament's Golden Ball as best player despite losing the final.

trajectory.title: Retirement from professional football
trajectory.description: Retired after 14 years at Bayern Munich with eight Bundesliga titles, six DFB-Pokals, and one Champions League, known as 'Der Titan.'

trajectory.title: CEO of Bayern Munich
trajectory.description: Became CEO of Bayern Munich, serving until May 2023, continuing his association with the club off the pitch.

name: Luis Suárez
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Eredivisie title and KNVB Cup with Ajax (2009-10 season) at age 22-23; won the 2011 Copa América with Uruguay at age 24; scored 111 goals in 159 appearances for Ajax before transferring to Liverpool in 2011.
starting_point: Born in Salto, Uruguay in 1987; moved to Montevideo at age seven with his parents and six brothers; grew up with little money, his family unable to afford football boots; joined Nacional's youth setup at 14.
current_position: Plays for Inter Miami in MLS; Uruguay's all-time top scorer with 69 goals in 142 appearances.

trajectory.title: Professional debut with Nacional
trajectory.description: Made his first-team debut for Nacional in the Copa Libertadores, scoring 10 goals in 27 matches as Nacional won the Uruguayan title.

trajectory.title: Move to Groningen
trajectory.description: Transferred to Dutch side Groningen, scoring 10 goals in 29 league matches and earning a move to Ajax.

trajectory.title: Signed for Ajax
trajectory.description: Joined Ajax for 6.75 million, beginning a prolific four-year stint where he scored 111 goals in 159 appearances.

trajectory.title: Eredivisie title and KNVB Cup with Ajax
trajectory.description: Won the Eredivisie title and KNVB Cup with Ajax in the 2009-10 season, establishing himself as one of Europe's top strikers.

trajectory.title: Copa América winner and transfer to Liverpool
trajectory.description: Won the 2011 Copa América with Uruguay (named player of the tournament) and transferred to Liverpool in January 2011.

trajectory.title: Premier League record and Barcelona transfer
trajectory.description: Equalled the Premier League scoring record with 31 goals in the 2013-14 season before transferring to Barcelona for 65 million pounds.

trajectory.title: Champions League and treble with Barcelona
trajectory.description: Won the Champions League, La Liga, and Copa del Rey with Barcelona, forming the lethal MSN trio with Messi and Neymar.

trajectory.title: Joined Inter Miami
trajectory.description: Joined Inter Miami in MLS, reuniting with former Barcelona teammate Lionel Messi.

name: Peter Gabriel
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Genesis at Charterhouse School in 1967 (age 17), released debut album From Genesis to Revelation in 1969 (age 19), and by age 26 had released multiple progressive rock classics including Nursery Cryme (1971), Foxtrot (1972), and Selling England by the Pound (1973).
starting_point: Born in Chobham, Surrey, England in 1950; son of an electrical engineer and dairy farm owner; attended Charterhouse School where he formed the band Garden Wall with schoolmate Tony Banks, which merged into Genesis in 1967.
current_position: Continues making music and activism work; inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as both a member of Genesis (2010) and as a solo artist (2014).

trajectory.title: Co-founded Genesis
trajectory.description: Formed Genesis with schoolmates at Charterhouse School, with the band signed by Jonathan King to Decca Records.

trajectory.title: Debut album 'From Genesis to Revelation'
trajectory.description: Released Genesis's debut album, produced during school summer break, marking the beginning of their recording career.

trajectory.title: 'Nursery Cryme' released
trajectory.description: Released 'Nursery Cryme,' the first of several progressive rock classics that defined Genesis's early sound.

trajectory.title: 'The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway'
trajectory.description: Released the concept double album 'The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway,' his last studio album with Genesis before departing in 1975.

trajectory.title: Solo debut and 'Solsbury Hill'
trajectory.description: Launched his solo career with the first of four self-titled albums, featuring the hit single 'Solsbury Hill.'

trajectory.title: 'So' and mainstream breakthrough
trajectory.description: Released the multi-platinum album 'So' featuring 'Sledgehammer,' which reached No. 1 and was accompanied by groundbreaking music videos.

trajectory.title: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Genesis
trajectory.description: Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Genesis, followed by solo induction in 2014.

trajectory.title: Album 'i/o' released
trajectory.description: Released 'i/o,' his first album of original material in 21 years, revealed one song at a time corresponding with full moons.

name: Mike Oldfield
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut album 'Tubular Bells' on 25 May 1973 at age 20, which became the first release on Virgin Records, sold over 2.7 million copies in the UK, reached No. 1 on the UK album chart, and was used in the film The Exorcist.
starting_point: Born in Reading, Berkshire, England in 1953; son of a general practitioner father and a homemaker mother; took up guitar at age ten, left school in his teens, and performed as a folk duo with his sister Sally before joining Kevin Ayers' band.
current_position: Retired from music; last album 'Return to Ommadawn' released in 2017; resides in the Bahamas.

trajectory.title: Left school and folk duo with sister
trajectory.description: Left school after an argument about his hair length and formed the folk duo the Sallyangie with his sister Sally, recording the LP 'Children of the Sun.'

trajectory.title: Joined Kevin Ayers' Whole World Band
trajectory.description: Joined Kevin Ayers' band as bassist and guitarist, recording three albums and using empty studio hours at Abbey Road to make his own demos.

trajectory.title: 'Tubular Bells' released
trajectory.description: Released debut album 'Tubular Bells' on May 25, 1973 as the first release on Virgin Records; it sold over 2.7 million copies in the UK and was used in 'The Exorcist.'

trajectory.title: 'Hergest Ridge' follows
trajectory.description: Released 'Hergest Ridge,' his second album, which like 'Tubular Bells' consisted of longform instrumental pieces and reached No. 1 in the UK.

trajectory.title: 'Ommadawn' released
trajectory.description: Released 'Ommadawn,' widely considered one of his finest albums, blending folk, rock, and world music influences.

trajectory.title: 'Crises' and 'Moonlight Shadow'
trajectory.description: Released 'Crises' featuring the worldwide hit single 'Moonlight Shadow' with vocalist Maggie Reilly, his most commercially successful period.

trajectory.title: 'Tubular Bells II' tops UK charts
trajectory.description: Released 'Tubular Bells II' after leaving Virgin for WEA, topping the British charts 19 years after the original.

trajectory.title: London Olympics opening ceremony performance
trajectory.description: Performed at the opening ceremony of the 2012 London Olympic Games, bringing 'Tubular Bells' to a global audience.

trajectory.title: Final album 'Return to Ommadawn'
trajectory.description: Released 'Return to Ommadawn,' his final studio album, before retiring from music.

name: Enrique Iglesias
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut album 'Enrique Iglesias' on November 21, 1995 at age 20, selling one million copies in three months with five number-one singles on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs chart, and won the Grammy Award for Best Latin Pop Performance in February 1997 at age 21.
starting_point: Born in Madrid, Spain in 1975 to singer Julio Iglesias and socialite Isabel Preysler; sent to Miami to live with his father after his grandfather's kidnapping; secretly borrowed money from his nanny to record a demo tape under the name 'Enrique Martinez.'
current_position: Continues recording and touring; has sold over 150 million records worldwide, making him one of the best-selling Latin artists of all time.

trajectory.title: Debut album release
trajectory.description: Released self-titled debut album 'Enrique Iglesias' on November 21, 1995, selling one million copies in three months with five number-one Billboard Hot Latin Songs singles.

trajectory.title: Grammy Award for Best Latin Pop Performance
trajectory.description: Won the Grammy Award for Best Latin Pop Performance in February 1997, establishing himself independently of his famous father.

trajectory.title: English-language crossover with 'Bailamos'
trajectory.description: Achieved crossover success with the single 'Bailamos,' which topped charts worldwide and launched his English-language career.

trajectory.title: 'Escape' and 'Hero' global hit
trajectory.description: Released the album 'Escape' featuring the global hit 'Hero,' cementing his status as a mainstream pop star beyond the Latin market.

trajectory.title: 'Euphoria' and bilingual success
trajectory.description: Released the bilingual album 'Euphoria' featuring hits 'I Like It' with Pitbull and 'Tonight (I'm Lovin' You),' both reaching the Billboard Top 5.

trajectory.title: Signed with Sony Music
trajectory.description: Parted with Universal Music Group after over a decade and signed with Sony Music for subsequent bilingual releases.

trajectory.title: 'Final (Vol. 2)' release
trajectory.description: Released 'Final (Vol. 2),' completing his intended final album project, capping a career with over 150 million records sold worldwide.
